newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rosneft awaits audit before possible Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Rosneft awaits audit before possible Eurobond.

text.p: Russian state oil holding company Rosneft intends to attract capital by issuing various financial instruments which could include Eurobonds, a senior Rosneft official said on Tuesday.
"We have many different plans but can't comment on them yet since nothing is concrete," First Deputy Chairman Rair Simonyan told Reuters.
Rosneft does not plan to carry out a Eurobond issue until it has gone through the necessary international audit, he added.
"We carried out a tender among the big six accounting firms, which Price Waterhouse won," he said, adding that the audit should be completed by midyear.
Preliminary data shows Rosneft's oil production grew in 1996 to 13.1 million tonnes from 12.8 million tonnes in 1995.
Last week Itar-Tass news agency quoted State Property Committee chairman Alfred Kokh as saying Russia would decide this month how to privatise state-owned oil company Rosneft.
Kokh said a 51 percent controlling stake would remain in state hands, while 23 to 24 percent would go to employees.
The remaining shares -- 25 to 26 percent -- would be sold through an open tender or at a special cash auction, he said.

Rosneft's privatisation has been delayed over quarrels with competitor SIDANKO (Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya) over ownership of crude oil producer Purneftegaz, which now belongs to Rosneft.
